text: By Vaught's test, which condition guarantees that a countable theory T with no finite models is complete?
choices: T has at least two non-isomorphic countable models
T is κ-categorical for some infinite cardinal κ (exactly one model of size κ up to isomorphism)
explanation: Vaught's theorem: a countable theory with no finite models that is κ-categorical for some infinite κ is complete — otherwise a sentence φ and its negation would each have a model of size κ (by Löwenheim–Skolem), contradicting categoricity. Option A is the opposite situation; decidability (C) and finite axiomatizability (D) are neither necessary nor sufficient for completeness here.
